AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: The pathology of allergic diseases involves type 2 immune cells, such as Th2, ILC2, and basophils exerting their effect by production of IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13. However, surface receptors that are specifically expressed on type 2 immune cells are less well documented. The aim of this investigation was to identify surface markers associated with type 2 inflammation.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Naïve human CD4+ T cells were short-term activated in the presence or absence of IL-4 and analyzed for expression of >300 cell-surface proteins. Ex vivo-isolated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from peanut-allergic (PA) and nonallergic subjects were stimulated (14-16 h) with peanut extract to detect peanut-specific CD4+ CD154+ T cells. Biopsies were obtained for transcriptomic analysis from healthy controls and patients with extrinsic or intrinsic atopic dermatitis (AD) and psoriasis.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Expression analysis of >300 surface proteins enabled identification of IL-4-upregulated surface proteins, such as CD90, CD108, CD109, and CD200R (CD200R1). Additional analysis of in vitro-differentiated Th0, Th1, and Th2 cultures identified CD200R as upregulated on Th2 cells. From ex vivo-isolated PBMCs, we found high expression of CD200R on Th2 and ILC2 cells and basophils. In PA subjects, the peanut-specific Th2 (CD154+ CRTh2+ ) cells expressed more CD200R than the non-allergen-specific Th2 (CD154- CRTh2+ ) cells. Moreover, costaining of CD161 and CD200R identified peanut-specific highly differentiated IL-4+ IL-5+ Th2 cells. Finally, transcriptomic analysis revealed upregulation of CD200R in lesional skin from subjects with an extrinsic AD phenotype compared to healthy skin.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: These results indicate that CD200R expression strongly correlates with Th2 pathology; though, the mechanism is as yet elusive.
